Sample type: Digoxin-free plasma (outdated blood-bank plasma) spiked with canrenone in vitro
Study method details: In vitro cross-reaction study; manual radioimmunoassay with 125-I tracer and gamma counting, no automated analyzer. Canrenone (Boehringer-Mannheim) made up in digoxin-free plasma across 0.125-125 mg/l; measured 'digoxin' read off each kit's own standard curve. The authors state that reporting the measured 'digoxin' level at each concentration 'is a much better way of expressing the cross-reaction than the often used and somewhat misleading concept of displacement at 50% binding'.
Additional sources of bias: 125 mg/l canrenone is roughly 30 times the highest in-vivo canrenone concentration reported in this same PDF (4.3 mg/l in a patient taking Soldactone/potassium canrenoate); spiked plasma, not native; coated-tube kits were additionally sensitive to serum albumin and globulin concentration (Table 7).
Notes: Units are transcribed as printed in the article (mg/l for canrenone, nmol/l for measured digoxin); the 1979 scan's text layer renders the lower-case l of the unit as the digit 1. Per the skill's conflict rule those cells are therefore not transcribed; only the unambiguous Summary statement is recorded here. The highest values visible in the extracted Table 6 columns are 3.57 (DPC), 5.61 (SPAC) and 2.54 (B-M) nmol/l, which do not match the Summary's 5.2 nmol/l exactly - an unresolved internal discrepancy. In-vivo context printed in the same paper (p82-83): maximal canrenone 0.40 mg/l after a single 200 mg spironolactone dose; steady-state minima up to 0.9 mg/l (200 mg/day), 1.7 mg/l (300 mg/day) and 2.6 mg/l (400 mg/day); and 4.3 mg/l in one congestive-heart-failure patient on potassium canrenoate. Discussion: 'In all kits, however, canrenone reacted with the antibody more than spironolactone' and 'care must be used when interpreting results from patients on either spironolactone or canrenoate therapy.' No percentage change can be computed because the baseline is printed as '<0.1 nmol/l' rather than a definite value.
